title: Theo and the Ghost
premise: Xanthe Voss translates secrets for a living — and buries the ones that would embarrass his handlers. When a realtor's listing exposes the interior of a supposedly untraceable safe house, Xanthe realizes someone from his own training program, the ghost he helped erase a decade ago, is selling him out piece by piece. To survive, he must turn interpreter of his own past, decoding the network that made him while the delegation he protects becomes collateral in someone else's war. The book ends with Xanthe burning the program's archive and choosing exile over duty, walking away from the woman he loves because loving her out loud would sign her death warrant.
about_author: Gideon Pemberton spent eleven years in logistics for humanitarian missions before turning to fiction, a career that taught him how paperwork kills. He writes from a different coastal town each year and refuses to confirm which ones.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Xanthe, mid-interpretation at a fractious Geneva summit, receives a real estate link showing photographs of a safe house only four people knew existed — including his own handwriting visible on a whiteboard. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: the cold drop from professional composure into hunted-animal awareness.

chapters.title: Cases No One Wants Attributed
chapters.summary: Flashback-laced chapter establishing Xanthe's double life: interpreter by day, deniable cleaner by night, and his careful, wordless intimacy with delegation security officer Mara Ilic. He verifies the listing is real and that the house is still occupied. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: dread braided with tenderness he can't afford.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Xanthe breaks into the listed property and finds it staged for sale with props from his own past — his training file, a photo of Mara. A dead handler in the basement has been arranged to look like Xanthe's work. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: horror of seeing himself framed by someone who knows his methods intimately.

chapters.title: The Program
chapters.summary: Through recovered documents, Xanthe reconstructs the Vellum Program: the unit that trained interpreters to be weapons and then dissolved them on paper. He identifies four surviving graduates and realizes the ghost is one of them. POV: alternating Xanthe and an unnamed second-person voice addressing him. Emotional beat: grief for the person he was manufactured to be.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Mara notices the handler's death and starts her own investigation, pulling threads that lead toward Xanthe. They circle each other at a delegation dinner, each hiding half a truth. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: love sharpened by suspicion — she trusts him and the evidence both.

chapters.title: The Second Graduate
chapters.summary: Xanthe tracks a fellow survivor, Odile, who reveals the ghost's motive: the program's principals are being collected one by one, and Xanthe is on the list. Odile offers an escape route he can't take without abandoning Mara. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: temptation of survival versus the pull of attachment.

chapters.title: Escrow
chapters.summary: The listing goes live publicly; intelligence services swarm the safe house, and the delegation's peace talks collapse in a staged leak Xanthe's ghost engineered. Mara confronts Xanthe with the frame-up evidence. POV: Mara, then Xanthe. Emotional beat: the relationship breaks open — betrayal confessed, love not withdrawn.

chapters.title: What the Ghost Wants
chapters.summary: Xanthe decodes the pattern: the ghost isn't killing graduates but forcing them to burn the program's archive before a buyer — the same buyer sabotaging the talks — can purchase the graduates themselves. The sale of the safe house was the message. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: reluctant admiration for an enemy who is right.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Climax. Xanthe infiltrates the archive handover at a decommissioned customs house, where the ghost — his first instructor, presumed dead — waits with the buyers. Xanthe torches the archive with both of them inside, sparing the ghost once as the man once spared him. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: rage, recognition, and mercy at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Sold
chapters.summary: The delegation limps home; the program's principals are exposed by the surviving fragments Xanthe chose to keep. Xanthe sends Mara a final translation — the one sentence he never said aloud — and vanishes into a new identity. POV: Mara reading his letter, then Xanthe at a border crossing. Emotional beat: love honored by absence, survival paid for in solitude.
